scenario: [LLOG.15.3]'s first bullet: an emit the literal break refutes compiles "unless it replaces a fact the rule itself matched, which [LLOG.11.9] refuses". The HonestPolitician shape. `corrupt` binds `Politician p where p.honest == true` and emits `Politician logical name: p.name honest: false`: the emit's key slot `name` is `p`'s own, and `honest: false` differs from the `true` the pattern requires, as LCYC.6.1.2 compares them. So the emit replaces the fact `p` matched ([LFAC.2.5.3]) and ends `corrupt`'s match at that emit; the `Politician` it makes would be withdrawn as it is made ([LLOG.15.1]). Being `logical`, it is refused with DS_VALIDATE_LOGICAL_EMIT_SELF_ENDING at the emit, line 17. The literal break still drops `corrupt -> hope` and `corrupt -> corrupt`, so the rule graph admits the program and the refusal is LLOG.11.9's. PATH PINNED: `dsc.validate`'s `llog_11_9_self_replacing`, comparing through `dsc.cycle`'s `llog_11_9_literal_breaks`. Control: LLOG.15.3_literal_flip_admitted, the same flip made by a rule that binds no `Politician`, which compiles. Twin: LLOG.15.3_withdraw_refused, these rules with `withdraw p` in place of the emit.
rules_ds:
schema Politician scope logical:
    name: String key
    honest: Bool mutable

schema Hope scope logical:
    name: String key

rule hope:
    Politician p where p.honest == true
->
    emit Hope logical name: p.name

rule corrupt:
    Politician p where p.honest == true
    Hope h where h.name == p.name
->
    emit Politician logical name: p.name honest: false
